assets.prompt: Photorealistic commercial photograph for a square 1:1 lifestyle advert: an everyday sunlit bathroom moment on an open stone ledge against a richly coloured tiled wall. Reference images: @front shows the exact product, a matte sage green hair conditioner bottle with a white flip-top cap. @back is for reference only. Reproduce the product exactly as in @front: the same shape, proportions, white matte flip-top cap with its thumb notch facing front, and the same soft-touch matte sage colour with no gloss. Keep the front label facing the camera, with every word spelled exactly and set in the same typefaces and positions as in @front: "VERDA", "Hydrating", "Conditioner", "detangles without weigh-down · 400 mL / 13.5 fl oz". The bottle stands upright in the left third of the foreground on a honey travertine ledge with visible natural pitting, in sharp focus, at about half the frame height, photographed in this scene rather than added to it. It casts a soft-edged shadow falling to the right that matches the sunlight, and leaves a true, subtle reflection in the honed stone. The scene is dry, so there is no water on the bottle or the ledge. Background: a wall of glazed terracotta zellige tile with slightly uneven, handmade tiles and gently varied glaze, a rich, saturated, earthy rust-orange clearly distinct from the sage bottle, kept soft by shallow depth of field but holding its full colour. The warm honey travertine contrasts in tone with the deeper terracotta wall. One prop only: a neatly folded thick white cotton terry towel behind and to the right of the bottle, lower than its shoulder. Lighting: hard, warm, low golden-hour sun from a window on the left falls across the bottle and ledge and throws crisp window-pane bar shadows across the tiles. Lit and shadowed areas differ clearly, and the warm highlights are never blown out on the label. Camera: level with the ledge at about mid-bottle height, straight on, 50mm lens at f/2.8, with only a thin sliver of the ledge top visible and no downward angle. Palette: terracotta, honey, sage and white, graded warm and full like an editorial magazine photograph. No other products, packaging or text, no people, no pale beige walls, no flat even light, no washed-out look.

Photorealistic commercial photograph for a square 2048x2048 social ad: an in-use hair care scene in a sunlit bathroom, shot straight on at ledge height. Reference images: @front shows the exact product, a matte sage green bottle with a white flip-top cap. @back is for reference only. Reproduce the product exactly as in @front, with the same shape, proportions, matte soft-touch sage finish, white flip-top cap with the thumb notch facing front, and colour. The front label faces the camera, with the words printed directly on the bottle in quiet cream lettering, spelled exactly and in the same typefaces and positions as @front: "VERDA", "Hydrating", "Conditioner", "detangles without weigh-down · 400 mL / 13.5 fl oz". The bottle stands upright in the left third of the foreground on a pale limestone ledge with visible natural pitting. It is in sharp focus, about half the frame height or slightly less, photographed in this scene rather than added to it. It casts a soft shadow falling to the right that matches the sunlight, with a true wet reflection in the damp stone beneath it. Fine water droplets and a few thin runs of water cover the bottle and cap. Scattered water beads sit on the limestone. In the right two thirds, in the mid-ground and clear of the bottle, a person is seen from behind and slightly to the side, with no face in frame. They wear a thick white cotton terry towel wrapped high around the shoulders. Both hands comb their fingers slowly through the long, wet lengths of dark hair, working a smooth, glossy white cream conditioner through the strands. The cream sits in silky streaks along the hair, and there is no foam or lather. The fingers are relaxed and natural, with natural skin texture, no jewellery, no painted nails and no tattoos. Nobody touches or overlaps the bottle. Background: a wall of rich, saturated ochre limewash plaster with soft mottling, kept soft through shallow depth of field but keeping its full warm colour. Crisp palm-leaf shadows fall across the wall. Lighting: hard, warm, low golden-hour sun from a window on the left, raking across the ledge and the bottle, with highlights warm and never blown out on the label. Shadows fall to the right, with strong contrast between lit and shadowed areas. Faint warm steam hangs in the air. Camera: level with the ledge at about mid-bottle height, so only a thin sliver of the ledge top is visible. Never look down onto the ledge. 50mm lens at f/2.8, with the foreground ledge and bottle sharp and the hands reading clearly. Palette: deep ochre, warm honey light, pale limestone, white cotton and sage. Editorial magazine colour grade, warm and full. No props. No other products, packaging or text. No face, no jewellery, no pale beige walls, no flat even light and no washed-out look.

A flat, warm cream (#f1eddf) backdrop with soft, even studio light and a very subtle paper grain. Nothing else in the frame.

Render this text in the image, spelled exactly as written, and no other text:
Headline, large: "Detangles without weigh-down"
Subline, much smaller, below it: "400 mL"

Set it in a clean geometric sans serif similar to Jost, regular weight, in deep sage green (#4f6147), left-aligned, vertically centred, inside the right half of the frame, with a right margin of at least 6% of the width. Leave the left half completely empty: a real pack is added there afterwards. Don't draw any bottle, jar or product. No boxes, effects, logos or watermarks.

The first reference image shows the scene with the product in place, the second shows the front of the product, and the third shows the back. A single continuous premium product shot with no cuts. The camera starts high above, looking down at the product from the top, then glides in one smooth orbit of about 220 degrees around it, descending gently as it travels, so the front, the side and the back each come into view. The product stays centred and perfectly still on the surface throughout. Its shape, proportions, cap, colour and finish never change, and every letter on its labels matches the reference images exactly. The surface and setting stay consistent with the scene as the camera moves. Soft natural light. No people, no hands and no added text.
